assessment: Inada and colleagues report results from a series of studies investigating the role of the neuropeptide oxytocin in regulating food intake and body weight. They used combinations of genetics and behavioral studies to demonstrate that oxytocin deletion results in increased food intake and body weight. They further show that deletion of the oxytocin receptor in the posterior hypothalamus causes a similar increase in food intake and body weight. Collectively, these studies support a role for the oxytocin system as a key regulator of energy balance.
